reviews.title: $80 for 10 Minutes of Use. A $20 Annual Plan Was Available. Buyer Beware.
reviews.text:
This app’s subscription pricing is absurd, and my experience has left me with absolutely zero trust in how they do business.

I signed up for a free trial, opened the app maybe twice, and used it for approximately 10 minutes TOTAL. I forgot to cancel before the trial expired. That’s my mistake, and I fully acknowledge it.

But then I was charged $80 for an annual subscription. I caught it the same day and immediately requested a cancellation and refund.

Denied.

Then I discovered something even more ridiculous. Hidden among the subscription options in my settings were multiple annual pricing tiers, including $20, $80, and options reaching $150. For the same app. With no obvious explanation for the enormous price differences.

Why was I charged $80 when a $20 annual option was available? What exactly justifies charging one customer FOUR TIMES as much? How is anyone supposed to make an informed purchasing decision with pricing this inconsistent?

I offered a completely reasonable compromise: refund the $60 difference and let me keep the $20 annual subscription. I wasn’t even asking for a free year.

Denied. Again.

So here’s the situation: I used this app for roughly 10 minutes, was charged $80, requested a refund the SAME DAY, discovered I could apparently have paid $20 for an annual subscription, and couldn’t even get the price difference refunded.

I understand how free trials work. I understand that I missed the deadline. What I don’t understand is why a company would offer such wildly inconsistent pricing and provide no reasonable path to resolve a charge disputed immediately.

This feels like a business model that benefits more from customers forgetting to cancel than from actually delivering $80 worth of value.

I can’t judge the app’s full functionality because I barely used it. But I can judge the subscription experience, and it’s one of the worst I’ve encountered.

Check every subscription option before you sign up. Apparently, $80 can buy you the same year that may be available for $20.

One star. Not because I forgot to cancel, but because of the pricing confusion and complete lack of a reasonable resolution afterward.

reviews.text:
Love the concept, started using a week or so ago. So far, things have been fun to play around with, whether it be the rankings and challenging myself to hit that next goal, or the tracker for your days worked out. 

ONLY thing so far that I need y’all to consider adding is a ranking system for the runners out there that throw in a run on the treadmill or outside. I get done with workouts and have seen progress just in this last week with my runs, but there’s nothing to showcase a medal or level up. Being competitive, I want to see where I stack up in that area as well, and I think it’d be a great addition. 

Otherwise, good work on the design! Great app to use so far.

reviews.title: Love this app but wished to see a few more things
reviews.text:
I have been loving this app so far! I am relatively new to the gym so it has really helped me structure my workouts and actually feel productive with my exercises. There are two main features i’d wish to see:
First, i’d love if we could pause our workout timers. I know there’s a workaround by just adjusting the final time, but it would be much easier if I were just able to pause it if i needed to take a break for the bathroom or whatever. 
Second, I wish there was a more clear way to log exercises that use individual limbs. For example, using dumbbells. I wish this because sometimes one arm isn’t as strong as the other so I end up either doing less reps or even less weight with one arm and I feel like I’m not able to accurately track my growth if I have to compromise by only logging the weaker one. 
Aside from these two things, I have been loving everything about the app and it would be a 5 stars for me if these two things were implemented!

reviews.title: How to Request a Refund
reviews.text:
If you’re like me, you also opted in to the try the pro version, but also got no notification that the trial period was up before they charged your card. Emailing or discord doesn’t work (I tried)

Scroll all the way down to the bottom of the app page, you’ll see “report a problem”. Click that button and sign into the page with your Apple ID. Use the drop down to select “Request a refund” then any of the options (I used “I didn’t mean to sign up for a subscription”). Then click next and select the subscription and submit your refund request.

It took like a day for them to send me an email saying they accepted my request.

Liftoff it would be great if your notification of the trial period ending soon actually worked :/

reviews.title: Does too much
reviews.text: The app is good, it certainly looks like it can help a lot of people out. I am not one of those people. I downloaded the app for one reason: to see the ranks I have for my workouts. I workout in a way I like: minimally structured, loose requirements, etc, and it’s worked great for months. I have a solid routine, diet, and everything needed to make progress. Liftoff doesn’t quite account for that, you only get 3 free rank calculations (plus one after downloading the app), and it annoys me because I have over 20 that I regularly do. This wouldn’t be a big problem if it weren’t for the fact that the app also wants to workout WITH me, not just track progress. Instead of being able to punch in numbers after a workout, it forces me to have it actually be integrated into the workout. And again, this isn’t a bad thing, it just isn’t my kind of app. I can’t reasonably rate this app lower than 4 stars. What I can say is that if you don’t have a well structured routine, this app is great. If you do have a well structure routine, I’d suggest against getting it.

I had the same situation where I was trying out the app, and saw an $80 payment go through. No cancelation reminder. The same day I requested to cancel it, providing valid reasons and prompt cancelation time. I have never had an issue with the Apple store providing a refund from more reputable apps, especially if it has only been ~1 day and I haven’t used the app or the subscription benefits. 

Don’t advertise notifying about canceling the subscription before the trial ends if you aren’t going to. I normally set my own personal reminders and this influenced me to just rely on the app. Thanks.

reviews.title: Meh
reviews.text: Devs have some significant gaps in anatomical knowledge. Also, the app rewards frequency and volume over intensity, making it fairly useless for strength athletes. Workouts recommended by the app are clearly not for strength athletes, i.e., the app recommends lots of single joint machine work and very little barbell work. It also doesn’t prioritize compound lifts at the beginning of the workout. Probably okay for calisthenics, endurance athletes, and bodybuilders. Definitely skip if you’re a powerlifter, Olympic lifter, or strongman.
